statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) in every hour of the CME weekend halt; Stress 25 (moderate); Confidence 70 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour of this window and Tail remains far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs 25 to 32 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack. No danger window is defined.
headline: Weekend halt, hour nineteen: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%), NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, unresolved hawkish Warsh repricing with the 2-year near 4.34% against a semiconductor-led Friday decline
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so every hour of this forecast window is a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August and the scheduled reopen falls about eight hours beyond the final slot of this window. Pre-halt evidence was re-verified against primary sources this run: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43 within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The dominant Friday driver remains Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, read as hawkish: the 2-year yield rose about 11 basis points to roughly 4.34 percent, its highest in a month, the 10-year moved to about 4.72 percent, and September rate-hike pricing carried in near 57 to 60 percent on fed funds futures against about 35 percent before the speech, with a prediction-market read near 48 percent. The equity decline was narrow rather than broad: the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.52 percent and the S&P 500 0.25 percent while semiconductors closed none of seven higher, led by Arm down 6.33 percent and Nvidia down 4.57 percent, and five of eight tracked megacaps advanced, with Amazon up 3.97 percent, Alphabet up 1.74 percent and Microsoft up 1.68 percent. The same repricing was expressed in a roughly 0.5 percent dollar gain and a 3.2 percent gold decline to near $4,456, while crude softened with WTI near $83.44 and Brent near $88.29, about 4 percent lower on the week as Middle East supply concern eased. Delayed cross-asset context showed Treasury futures lower across the curve and the volatility future up 1.64 percent, consistent with that read but not usable as live price-path evidence. Weekend headline flow through the assessment cutoff has been thematic rather than index-moving, with no verified geopolitical or policy discontinuity. Because Tail measures a persistent no-retracement price path and no venue is open to produce one, Tail is 5 in every hour of this window and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with no danger window; Stress runs 25 to 32 in the moderate band purely as a measure of information waiting to be priced at the reopen, and Confidence steps down from 70 to 64 as a function of tape age rather than conflicting evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the final five hours of Friday's cash session and the first nineteen hours of the weekend halt. The mode was event/whipsaw as the Jackson Hole keynote hit the tape, and Tail peaked at 22 with Stress at 64 in the 16:00 to 19:00 UTC block; the mapped policy state never exceeded WATCH because retracements kept occurring throughout the repricing. After the 20:00 UTC cash close the readings decayed quickly, Tail from 12 to 5 and Stress from 52 to 25, as the venue entered its weekend closure and the mode reverted to normal. Every hour of this window has a published assessment. The nineteen halt hours sit at a flat Tail of 5 with Stress in the low to mid twenties, and Confidence steps down from 88 to 71 purely as a function of tape age.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form; Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON throughout with no danger window, and the dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress runs 25 to 32 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates: the unresolved hawkish policy read with the 2-year near 4.34 percent and September hike odds around 57 to 60 percent, Friday's narrow semiconductor-led decline with Arm down 6.33 percent and Nvidia down 4.57 percent against five of eight megacaps higher, the roughly 3.2 percent drop in gold and 0.5 percent dollar gain that expressed the same repricing, the softer crude path near $83 WTI, Broadcom results scheduled after the close on 2 September, and the 1 to 4 September data stack running from ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS through to the August employment report. Confidence steps down from 70 to 64 across the window as the pre-halt tape ages. The scheduled reopen at 22:00 UTC on 30 August falls about eight hours beyond the final slot, so any gap, retracement or one-way structure that forms there is conditional here and will be scored on observed evidence in a later cycle.
